sections.h2: What makes Berwyn different from other Chicago-area suburbs for sellers?
sections.html:
Berwyn is a dense inner-ring suburb in Cook County, packed into 3.90 square miles with Oak Park to the north, Cicero to the east, Stickney to the south, and Lyons, Riverside, North Riverside and Forest Park to the west. Its nickname is the City of Homes, and the housing reflects it: small bungalows on the north side around Roosevelt and Cermak roads, larger houses toward the south, and many duplexes and three-unit buildings scattered between.

The ground matters to anyone buying here. Before settlement the area was grassy marshland, with Mud Lake reaching nearly to today's southern border, and the south end flooded regularly in heavy rain during its early years. A sand and gravel beach ridge from ancient Lake Chicago runs along Riverside Drive. A buyer's inspector will look at basements and sewer laterals closely, so a seller with old flooding or backup history should gather repair records and any sewer scope reports before listing.

sections.h2: How dense and how costly is Berwyn housing?
sections.html:
Census Bureau estimates put Berwyn at 55,001 residents on July 1, 2025, down 3.9 percent from an April 2020 base of 57,235. Its density was 14,664.4 people per square mile in the 2020 count.

sections.h2: What does the City of Berwyn require when a house changes hands?
sections.html:
Berwyn runs its own transfer paperwork through the Collections and Licensing office and the Compliance Department at City Hall, 6700 W. 26th Street. The city's checklist for quit claim transfers shows what the office looks at, and sellers on a regular sale should ask the same departments which items apply to them.

  • Building: a property inspection is required when all parties are coming off title, any fines or liens must be paid, and open permits must be closed out.
  • Police: parking tickets and fines must be paid in full.
  • Water: the water bill balance must be current.
  • Collector: bring the original deed that will be recorded with Cook County, the completed Berwyn Declaration form and a payment of $100.00, payable to the City of Berwyn by cash, check, money order or credit card.
  • Trusts and corporations: add the trust agreement or corporate papers only if the property is coming out of the trust or corporation, and add an Attorney's Certification form when someone is added to or removed from title.

City stamps are processed at the counter or by mail on four weekdays (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) between 9 a.m. and half past four, and on Tuesday until half past seven in the evening. Mailed packets need a return envelope with postage. The Compliance Department number is (708) 788-2660, extensions 6445 or 6449.

sections.h2: How does a Berwyn certificate of compliance and occupancy work?
sections.html:
Berwyn issues certificates of compliance and occupancy after a city inspection, and the fee depends on the type of property. For residential buildings the city's fee sheet lists $100.00 for a single-family house, $125.00 for two to three units, $175.00 for four to six units, and $70.00 for each unit over six.

Inspections are scheduled in person at the first-floor Compliance Department window in City Hall, with payment due when you schedule and no exceptions. Cash, check, money order and credit cards are accepted. An inspection report stays valid for six months from the inspection date, so time it close to your target closing rather than months ahead. The service window opens at 9 a.m. every weekday, closes at 5 p.m. on four of them, and stays open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays.

Ask the Compliance Department whether your particular sale needs a certificate, because the answer can depend on the building type and who is on title. Buyers who plan to rehab a property often accept the inspection list as part of an as-is price.

sections.h2: What building permit rules should Berwyn sellers know?
sections.html:
The Building Permits Department says permits go out only until half past four on most weekdays and half past seven on Tuesdays. Applications can be submitted in person or emailed to buildingpermits@berwyn-il.gov, and incomplete applications are not sent for director review. Homeowners may do some non-commercial repairs themselves under the city's Work By Owner handout, but the city publishes guides on what needs a permit and on hiring contractors.

Codes the city lists as applicable include the 2024 International Residential Code, the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code, the Illinois State Plumbing Code 2014 and the 2021 Illinois Energy Conservation Code. If a prior owner finished a basement or added a bathroom without a permit, resolving it can take time, so ask for your address's permit file early.

sections.h2: What happens at the Cook County Clerk when a Berwyn deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Cook County deeds are recorded by the Clerk's Recording Division at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 120, in person or by mail. A deed needs the property index number (PIN), the full legal description, the property address, a mail-to address, the grantee's name and address, the name and address for future tax bills, and city, state and county transfer tax declarations and stamps or a stated exemption. The Clerk tells filers to check with the municipality for its own requirements, so Berwyn's own declaration and payment are a separate step before recording.

The Clerk's page prints the stamp history for Illinois: since September 15, 1989, stamps are $0.75 per $500.00, split into $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Only title companies may e-record deeds that carry consideration, while fully exempt deeds can be e-recorded by other filers. A document that misses the Clerk's format standards is charged an additional fee equal to the normal recording fee.

sections.h2: How do Cook County assessments and tax bills work for Berwyn homes?
sections.html:
Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year, and a reassessment notice shows the PIN, characteristics, estimated market value and assessed value. The Assessor's page says residential assessed value equals 10 percent of fair market value, then a state equalizer and exemptions are applied. Appeals can be filed with the Assessor or the Cook County Board of Review.

The Cook County Treasurer mails two installments a year. The Treasurer's due-date page shows that tax year 2025 installments were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, tax year 2024 installments were due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025, and tax year 2023 installments were due March 1, 2024 and August 1, 2024. The Assessor notes that the first installment is exactly 55 percent of the prior year's total. Because those dates move from year to year, read the Treasurer's page or your own bill before choosing a closing day. Exemptions listed by the Treasurer include homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, persons with disabilities and home improvement.

faqs.q: Does Berwyn require a city inspection to sell my house?
faqs.a: It depends on the transaction, so ask the Compliance Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6445 or 6449. The city's quit claim checklist requires an inspection when all parties come off title, and its fee sheet lists certificates of compliance and occupancy at $100.00 for a single-family house.

faqs.q: How long is a Berwyn inspection report good for?
faqs.a: Six months from the inspection date. If closing slips past that window, plan on a new inspection and a new fee.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate on a Cook County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk's page prints $0.75 per $500.00 of value, made up of $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Berwyn adds its own declaration and a city payment, so ask the Collector's office what applies to your transaction.

faqs.q: Where do I pay water and parking fines before closing?
faqs.a: Contact the Water Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6463 or 6466 for the balance, and the Police Department at (708) 795-5600 for parking tickets. The city's checklist says both must be current.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Berwyn house with open permits?
faqs.a: Open permits must be closed out for a transfer to be processed, according to the city's checklist. Ask the Building Department for the permit file, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to a buyer who will complete it.
